title: This Thing, These Things
summary: Use sa a and sa yo to point out things and combine them with ownership in a short exchange.

sketchBlocks.title: sa a
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Use **sa a** after a noun for “this” or “that.”

For example:

**machin sa a** — this car / that car

The demonstrative comes after the noun.

segments.text: The demonstrative comes after the noun.

help.concept: using sa a after a noun
help.hint_1: Use the noun phrase pattern introduced in the lesson.
help.hint_2: Pay attention to what comes before or after the noun.

sketchBlocks.title: sa yo
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
Use **sa yo** after a noun for “these” or “those.”

For example:

**machin sa yo** — these cars / those cars

Homework examples also combine this pattern with ownership.

segments.text: Homework examples also combine this pattern with ownership.

help.concept: using sa yo after a noun
help.hint_1: Use the noun phrase pattern introduced in the lesson.
help.hint_2: Pay attention to what comes before or after the noun.

sketchBlocks.title: Jan and Mari sort their things
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
**Jan:** Mari, liv sa a se pou ou.

**Mari:** Mèsi, Jan. Kaye sa yo se pou ou.

**Jan:** Mèsi.

This combines demonstratives, possession, and familiar polite language without adding a new question pattern.
